audits.title: EP.TU.785Quality Improvement Project: Improving Oxygen therapy prescription in surgical inpatients
audits.standard: National (BTS) and local standards that oxygen is prescribed; SMART aim to increase prescribing by 20% each month
audits.setting: Surgical wards, large city hospital (Birmingham Heartlands Hospital)

cycle1.result: 78% of patients not prescribed oxygen (22% prescribed).

audits.intervention: PDSA cycle 1: departmental poster (seminar with induction material and system checklist notification planned for later cycles).

cycle2.result: Mean percentage prescribed increased from 22% to 60%.

audits.other_findings: Later results (>75% and >95%) are projections, not measurements.
audits.citation: Hamid M, Al-Saket L, Rawashdeh A, Sudarsanam R. EP.TU.785Quality Improvement Project: Improving Oxygen therapy prescription in surgical inpatients. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab311.102.

audits.title: Prescribing oxygen therapy. An audit of oxygen prescribing practices on medical wards at North Shore Hospital, Auckland, New Zealand.
audits.standard: Oxygen should be prescribed in the medication chart
audits.setting: Medical wards, North Shore Hospital, Auckland

cycle1.result: Only 8% of patients receiving oxygen had it prescribed; 75% of prescriptions were inadequate.

audits.citation: Boyle M, Wong J. Prescribing oxygen therapy. An audit of oxygen prescribing practices on medical wards at North Shore Hospital, Auckland, New Zealand. N Z Med J. 2006;119(1238):U2080. PMID: 16868577.

audits.title: Audit of oxygen use in emergency ambulances and in a hospital emergency department.
audits.standard: Joint Royal Colleges Ambulance Liaison Committee (JRCALC) guidance on oxygen use
audits.setting: Ambulance service and emergency department 'majors' section of a university hospital (Salford Royal)

cycle1.result: SpO2 recorded for 90% of patients (remainder of results truncated in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Baseline audit before new national emergency oxygen guidelines; oxygen use was suboptimal, especially in COPD.
audits.citation: Hale KE, Gavin C, O'Driscoll BR. Audit of oxygen use in emergency ambulances and in a hospital emergency department. Emerg Med J. 2008;25(11):773-776. doi:10.1136/emj.2008.059287. PMID: 18955625.

audits.title: A Two-Cycle Audit of Oxygen Prescription in Hospitalised Patients Receiving Supplemental Oxygen: A Retrospective Study.
audits.standard: National guidelines and local policy requiring a documented oxygen prescription with target saturation range (British Thoracic Society)
audits.setting: Acute medical and general medical wards, Victoria Hospital Kirkcaldy (NHS Fife)

cycle1.period: First and second weeks of November 2024
cycle1.result: 19% had an appropriate oxygen prescription documented on the medication chart.

audits.intervention: Poster campaign on oxygen prescription requirements and a mass email reminder to resident doctors.
audits.other_findings: Most patients lacked any formal documentation of oxygen therapy; rotation of resident doctors every four months was identified as a barrier to sustained improvement.
audits.citation: Thinn PP, Swe TH, Delicata M. A Two-Cycle Audit of Oxygen Prescription in Hospitalised Patients Receiving Supplemental Oxygen: A Retrospective Study. Cureus. 2025;17(12):e98732. doi:10.7759/cureus.98732. PMID: 41510482.

audits.title: Time for change in practice of in-patient oxygen therapy: a period-limited, multidimensional approach to improve oxygen prescription compliance: quality improvement project at Hamad General Hospital, Qatar.
audits.standard: British Thoracic Society guidelines (2017): oxygen must be prescribed; target 80% compliance with valid oxygen prescription
audits.setting: Acute medical assessment unit and general medical wards, Hamad General Hospital

cycle1.result: No patient had a valid oxygen prescription on the electronic system; duration documented in 25% (18/72), target range 45.8% (33/72) and indications 42% (30/72).

audits.intervention: Eight PDSA cycles over 16 weeks: educational sessions for residents, fellows and nurses; introduction of electronic prescription; emails, posters and flyers; nurse-led reminders; re-enforced teaching for new residents.

cycle2.result: Electronic oxygen prescription 93%, indications 85%, target oxygen saturation 86% and wean-off plan 80%.

audits.other_findings: Oxygen was initially started by communication order only.
audits.citation: Rose S, Sardar S, Sasi S, Al Mohanadi DHSH, Al-Mohammed AAAA, Zahid M. Time for change in practice of in-patient oxygen therapy: a period-limited, multidimensional approach to improve oxygen prescription compliance: quality improvement project at Hamad General Hospital, Qatar. BMJ Open Qual. 2021;10(4):e001574. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2021-001574. PMID: 34815252.

audits.title: A Quality Improvement Study to Improve Oxygen Prescription in the PICU of a Tertiary Care Centre in Delhi, India.
audits.setting: Paediatric intensive care unit, tertiary care centre, Delhi
audits.intervention: QI team, root cause analysis and four PDSA cycles (specific changes not described).

cycle2.result: 91.42% valid prescriptions in the fourth PDSA cycle.

audits.other_findings: Valid prescription rates were 62.07%, 79.51% and 81.81% in PDSA cycles 1 to 3; 75% of staff knew target saturation.
audits.citation: Shukla A, Bhaskar V, Batra P. A Quality Improvement Study to Improve Oxygen Prescription in the PICU of a Tertiary Care Centre in Delhi, India. Cureus. 2023;15(8):e43332. doi:10.7759/cureus.43332. PMID: 37700982.

audits.title: Automated audit of hospital oxygen use devised during the COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.standard: British Thoracic Society oxygen audit standards (valid oxygen prescription and saturation within prescribed target range)
audits.setting: Salford Royal Hospital, Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust; hospital-wide wards excluding critical care

cycle1.period: late 2019 onwards (51 audits, including COVID-19 waves)
cycle1.result: Over 51 automated audits of 34 352 sets of observations, 6.0% involved oxygen use and 88.6% of these had a valid oxygen prescription.

audits.other_findings: Oxygen use rose to 10.4% in the first COVID-19 wave, 10.6% in the second and 7.4% in the third (Omicron) wave, returning to baseline after each. The paper describes a bespoke automated EMR-based audit with a traffic-light display.
audits.citation: O'Driscoll R, Bakerly ND. Automated audit of hospital oxygen use devised during the COVID-19 pandemic. BMJ Open Respir Res. 2023;10(1):e001866. doi:10.1136/bmjresp-2023-001866. PMID: 38154912.
